label: 2-4 steps after an early o (o as 1st or 2nd original token)
explanation: Fires on early original-phase steps (t=2..4) in sequences whose first or second original token is the letter o, i.e. a short delayed echo of an early o. The identity of the current input does not matter. If o is the first token it fires at t=2,3,4; if o is the second token it fires at t=3,4. Activation peaks at t=3-4 (t=3 alone carries about 48% of the mass, t=2 is weaker at about 0.37 of max), and the largest activations come from sequences that start with o (often o o o). It also fires weakly on the delimiter step when L<=4. It is essentially silent at t=0,1, at t>=6, and throughout the copy phase. Leftover misses are weak: t=5 when o is the second token (left out of the predicate because about half of those steps are inactive), and sparse low activations after an o in position 2 or later.

issues: Reproduced the test scores: P 0.899, R 0.834, F1 0.865, mass recall 0.954.

The phase claims hold. The copy phase is essentially silent (phase>=2 has 38 active steps on dev, mass recall 0.0003). Activity drops to almost nothing after t=5: 468 active steps at t=6, 10 at t=7 and none after that. t=0 and t=1 are fully silent. t=3 carries 48.2% of the mass.
The sub-cases check out. orig(0)=o at t=2 has precision 1.00, and at t=3 0.997. orig(1)=o at t=3 has precision 0.91. The t=4 cases are weaker, at about 0.80.

One small systematic false-positive class: when L=4, step t=4 is the delimiter, and there the precision is only 0.32. Restricting the predicate to phase==0 raises test F1 only slightly, from 0.865 to 0.868. The explanation's 'fires weakly on the delimiter when L<=4' is roughly right but slightly overstated.

The misses are systematic but weak, and the explanation already mentions them. orig(2)=o at t=4-5 has precision 0.27 and holds 4.7% of the mass. orig(1)=o at t=5 has precision 0.30 and 1.9% of the mass. Adding either to the predicate lowers F1 (0.809 and 0.845).
The lowest activation quartile is only 41% covered. These are weak echoes of an o at later positions; they hold little mass and are acceptable.
